# ERBB2 (erb-b2 receptor tyrosine kinase 2) 
 
Entrez ID: 2064 
Genomic coordinate (GRCh38, provider default): 17:39687914-39730426 (strand: 1) 
UniProt: P04626 
Type: protein-coding 
Source: NCBI Gene / MyGene.info 
 
## Summary (NCBI Gene) 
 
This gene encodes a member of the epidermal growth factor (EGF) receptor family of receptor tyrosine kinases. This protein has no ligand binding domain of its own and therefore cannot bind growth factors. 
Diseases: non-small cell lung carcinoma, cancer, gastric cancer, breast carcinoma, gastric adenocarcinoma 
Drugs: MM-111, KBP5209, LAPATINIB DITOSYLATE, CANERTINIB DIHYDROCHLORIDE, PERTUZUMAB

## Protein (UniProt) 
 
- Accession: P04626 
- Name: Receptor tyrosine-protein kinase erbB-2 
- Also known as: MLN 19, Metastatic lymph node gene 19 protein, Proto-oncogene Neu, Proto-oncogene c-ErbB-2, Tyrosine kinase-type cell surface receptor HER2, p185erbB2 
- Length: 1255 aa 
- Isoforms (6): ERBB2 (1255 aa), CTF-611, CTF-687, 4, 5, B 
- Function: Protein tyrosine kinase that is part of several cell surface receptor complexes, but that apparently needs a coreceptor for ligand binding. Essential component of a neuregulin-receptor complex, although neuregulins do not interact with it alone. GP30 is a potential ligand for this receptor. Regulates outgrowth and stabilization of peripheral microtubules (MTs). Upon ERBB2 activation, the MEMO1-RHOA-DIAPH1 signaling pathway elicits the phosphorylation and thus the inhibition of GSK3B at cell membrane. This prevents the phosphorylation of APC and CLASP2, allowing its association with the cell membrane. In turn, membrane-bound APC allows the localization of MACF1 to the cell membrane, which is required for microtubule capture and stabilization
